correctness.rationale: The count, cubic coefficient and direction-tagged mark check out. For 1+ε<√2 the lattice has no unit-distance triangle, so each occupied pair is unique and is horizontal or vertical. Translational unfolding for each of these two directions gives its covariogram mass, not twice that mass. Center P at zero: P−P=2P and strict convexity of the Euclidean ball forces the finitely many points on its unit circle to be antipodal vertex differences. In a fixed small neighborhood of each such vertex, both overlap pieces are exactly their opposing translated tangent cones. In ray coordinates (1,m⁻),(1,m⁺), the intersection is the box with sides s₋=(m⁺bₓ−bᵧ)/h and s₊=(bᵧ−m⁻bₓ)/h if both are nonnegative. The determinant is h, giving the exact product of the two positive parts divided by h. In the localized angular patch the support constraint |sin α|≤max(|m⁻|,|m⁺|)(ε+1−cos α) forces |α|=O_P(ε) by absorbing its O_P(α²) term. Each endpoint solves −sin α=m(ε+1−cos α) and equals −mε+O_P(ε²). On the resulting fixed compact t=α/ε scale the positive-part formula differs from ε²(m⁺+t)₊(−m⁻−t)₊/h uniformly by O_P(ε³), including the boundary of the shifted interval. Its integral in α is h²ε³/6+O_P(ε⁴). Two antipodal alignments for each of two unoriented coordinate axes give 4/(2π) times that mass. Normalizing after u=(t+m⁺)/h gives 6u(1−u); reversal reflects the interval and its slope labels. Across distinct diameter pairs some angle windows can coincide, so the conditioning is on the encounter's specified direction as well as the orientation neighborhood, not the angle alone. This is the direction-tagged reading of the frozen statement. The positive coefficient and A≤π/4 give positive mass on all three atoms for sufficiently small positive ε. Independent 45-digit integration for the diameter-one rectangle of sides 4/5 and 3/5 used the exact translated intersection (4(1+ε)/5−cos θ)(3(1+ε)/5−sin θ) on [acos(4(1+ε)/5),asin(3(1+ε)/5)] in one quadrant. Total cubic ratios at ε=.01,.002,.0004 were 1.007685013, 1.001515641, 1.000302292. In the small-gap case the rescaled mark's first two moments were .499918559 and .299945394 (limits 1/2 and 3/10). This checks normalization and a nonsymmetric angular window, not the general proof. The supplied checker was inspected, not executed.

Their exact cross covariogram, including the zero region, is a determinant times the product of the two positive ray coordinates. Substitution at those arcs into the earlier conditional lattice identity exhausts the outcomes; other assumptions of the smooth curvature formula are irrelevant to this implication.

evidence: Let B have columns r₋=(1,m⁻), r₊=(1,m⁺), det B=h. The exact prior cone overlap for A=C, −B_cone=C yields h s₋₊s₊₊ for displacement B(s₋,s₊): in those coordinates it is the orthant intersected with its reflection about (s₋,s₊)/2. Equivalently the mixed derivative in these ray coordinates is h in the positive quadrant and the area vanishes on its axes.

On the unit-vector arc around a contact for (1+ε)P, substitute displacement ((1+ε)−cos α,−sin α). The exact two-direction unfolding thus gives on each tagged branch dPr=(2π)⁻¹h⁻¹[m⁺((1+ε)−cos α)+sin α]₊[−sin α−m⁻((1+ε)−cos α)]₊ dα. Its support is O(ε), and ordinary Taylor expansion on α=εt gives ε²(m⁺+t)₊(−m⁻−t)₊/h with uniform O(ε³) error. Integrating dα and taking the four alignments gives the cubic coefficient and O(ε⁴) remainder; with u=(t+m⁺)/h, dividing the same density by its integral gives the Beta(2,2) mark.

evidence: For X,Y independent uniform in P, the difference density at z is g_P(z)/A². With s=(1+ε)⁻¹, the distance density is f(s)=s/A² times the angle integral of g_P(sω). Thus for small ε, p₂(ε)=(1+ε)²A² f(s)/(πs). Conditioning on the difference length s with the covariogram as the angular density gives the same local angular mark after fixing an oriented branch; this uses the angle-resolved density, not just f(s).

The radial covariogram is also the isotropic correlation of the polygon (up to area normalization); integrating the invariant chord tail recovers it by the directional derivative identity in Bianchi Eq. (2).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A result for the distance density or isotropic correlation would cover the unmarked probability after the exact normalization change. A radial mean alone cannot establish an angle-conditioned law. The pointwise covariogram result supplies that missing information.

evidence: Bäsel arXiv:1204.2707v2 §§2–4 gives exact even-regular-polygon terminal chord formulas. With diameter 1, β=π/n and K=n/2−1, Eq. (6) gives α_K(s)=asin(cos β/s)−(π/2−β)=cot β(1−s)+O((1−s)²). The integrand q_K(s,ψ) of Eq. (5) is cot β(1−s)/2+O(ψ²). Integrating on [0,α_K(s)] and multiplying by 2n as in §3 Case 2 yields invariant long-chord measure n cot²β(1−s)²+O((1−s)³). Integrating in s yields half the full angle integral of the covariogram. The exact lattice conversion then gives the frozen regular-even coefficient 2n cot²β/(3π).

The general-polygon isotropic correlation formula is advertised by Ciccariello DOI 10.1063/1.3227660; the primary abstract and his related arXiv:1006.1496v1 §2 give scope and triangle formulas, respectively. No exact general endpoint table from that article is used as decisive evidence here.

originality.rationale: The exact prior angle-resolved lattice unfolding and the exact prior polygon covariogram reduction at a difference-body vertex together cover the main claim by direct specialization. The implication is stronger than a shared proof strategy: the two sources already give the exact pointwise mass for the same tagged collision branch at every sufficiently small gap, via the elementary opposing-cone case. Expanding that explicit density on its support, integrating, and normalizing recovers the frozen coefficient, remainder and mark with no new structural lemma. This does not assert that the Beta name or the coefficient in this notation appears verbatim in either source.
residual_risks: No claim about who first stated the endpoint coefficient or the conditional Beta law verbatim. The rejection rests on demonstrated mathematical implication from the inspected exact results.
The full Ciccariello 2009 and Gates 1987 papers were not available in inspected material; they may further sharpen the historical attribution. No negative claim is made about their contents.
The degeneracy of coinciding angle windows across different coordinate axes is handled by the stated branch tag; no Beta law for arbitrary unions of untagged windows is inferred.

value.rationale: The diameter threshold and direction mark are natural and the clean coefficient is useful as a worked example. But under the narrow exact-invariant standard, the frozen package supplies no surviving nonmechanical result: known angle-resolved unfolding and exact vertex covariograms already fix both claimed outputs, and the passage to the stated constants is a compactly supported quadratic Taylor calculation. No quantitative uniform family, different regime, or further independent structural theorem is proved in the assigned record.
